site_article.headline: How to use Genspark AI for free: slides, credits and limits
site_article.dek: Genspark's free plan gives you 100 credits a day. Here is how to spend them on a slide deck, what each task costs and what the free plan will not let you do.

paragraphs.text: Genspark is an AI workspace built around agents: you describe what you want, and it plans and builds a finished file, such as a slide deck, a spreadsheet or a document. You can use it for free. A free account gets 100 credits a day, and a 10 page slide deck costs about 100 credits on the Standard tier. The catch is that free accounts cannot download or export files, so a free deck lives inside Genspark as a link.

Genspark has grown well past its start as an AI search engine. Its help center lists more than 20 products, including Super Agent for open ended tasks, AI Slides, AI Sheets, AI Docs, Genspark Code for building apps, AI Meeting Notes, Call For Me, which places phone calls for you, plus image, video and music tools. Lindy, which sells a competing agent platform, describes Super Agent as the piece that routes a request to the right tools and returns a finished result.
What the free plan gives you

According to Genspark's Membership Plans page, the free plan includes 100 credits per day up to a lifetime allowance, 1 GB of AI Drive storage and limited access to models and agents. The Credits Guide adds that once the lifetime allowance is used, the daily refill stops, but whatever balance is left still works until it runs out. Images made in AI Image on the free plan carry a watermark.

For AI Slides, a free account can build a deck, present it and share a link. Export, Creative mode and Make a Copy need a paid plan. Super Agent also needs a minimum credit balance before it will start a turn on the free plan.
How to build a slide deck in Genspark

paragraphs.title: 1. Open AI Slides
paragraphs.text: Create a free account, then open AI Slides under New in the sidebar. Lindy's walkthrough says no credit card is needed to sign up. Use Super Agent instead when the task is open ended and you do not know yet what the output should be.

paragraphs.title: 2. Set the three modes before you type
paragraphs.text: Genspark shows three pickers: Professional or Creative, Auto Mode or Guide Mode, and Standard or Ultra. They lock for the project after your first send, so choose first. On the free plan, stay on Professional and Standard. Creative needs a paid plan, and Professional is the only mode where you can edit text boxes later, because Creative slides are single generated images.

paragraphs.title: 3. Describe the deck and attach your files
paragraphs.text: Say who the deck is for, how long it should be and the one point it has to make. Attach source files with the + button in the prompt box. Write the prompt in the language you want the slides in, because the prompt's language sets the deck's language.

paragraphs.title: Prompt: a short deck from your own notes
paragraphs.text: Make a [8] slide presentation for [my team's Monday meeting] about [our Q4 sales results]. Use only the numbers in the attached file. One idea per slide, a chart where the data supports it, and a final slide with three next steps. Plain, professional style.

paragraphs.title: 4. Send, then fix one thing at a time
paragraphs.text: After you send, the agent plans the deck and builds it page by page on a canvas next to the chat. To change one part, use Select to pick an element, or Draw to mark a spot with a pen, marker or box and type what should change, then send the queued edits. History keeps save points, so you can restore an earlier version.

paragraphs.title: 5. Check the facts, then share or export
paragraphs.text: Use Verify content to check the deck before anyone sees it. Then use Share for a link or Present to show it. On a paid plan, Export in the header saves the deck as PDF, PowerPoint or Google Slides; Google Slides needs a one time connection to your Google account.
Manual edits and exports do not cost credits, and failed runs are refunded automatically. Stopping a run halfway does not get your credits back, so let a run finish before you judge it.
What tasks cost in credits

Genspark's AI Slides page says Standard starts at 10 credits per page and Ultra at 100 credits per page, so a 10 slide deck is about 100 credits on Standard and about 1,000 on Ultra. Charts and rewritten text can cost more than that floor. On the free plan, that means roughly one Standard deck a day, and an Ultra deck is out of reach.

The Credits Guide does not give a fixed price for most tasks. It says cost depends on the model tier, text length, image resolution, video length, audio length, the number of outputs and how complex the task is, and that regenerations, agent retries and long chats each add to it. You can see your balance and usage log from the Credits item in the bottom left menu, though the log can lag by a few hours.
Video burns through a free allowance fastest, according to Lindy's review. If you only have the free plan, spend your credits on slides, documents and research, and leave video for later.
Paid plans, and when they are worth it

Plus costs $24.99 a month, or $19.99 a month billed yearly, and includes 10,000 credits a month and 50 GB of storage. Pro costs $249.99 a month, or $199.99 a month billed yearly, with 125,000 credits and 1 TB. Team is $40 per seat a month, or $35 billed yearly. Paid plans also get a weekly Free Quota for Standard mode in Super Agent, AI Slides, AI Sheets, AI Docs and Deep Research that does not use credits. Monthly credits do not roll over.

For most people, the free plan is a fair test drive, not a working setup. It shows you whether Genspark's decks are good enough for you, but without export you cannot take a deck into PowerPoint or hand in a PDF. If you make slides every week, Plus is the plan where Genspark becomes useful.
Where Genspark falls short

Genspark's own help center lists several limits: a PowerPoint export can look different from the canvas and swap fonts, scanned PDFs without a text layer can come through empty, and AI Chat and AI Image have a separate five hour usage window that buying more credits does not lift. eesel, which sells a competing AI product, reports that the most common complaint from paying users is credits burning faster than expected on failed or retried tasks.
Turn on the Ask First setting on the usage page if you are on a paid plan. It asks before a task starts spending credits instead of the free quota.
